items.title: Graded ring module bimodule and internal shift
items.statement: Over a commutative ground ring k placed in degree zero, take unital associative Z-graded k-algebras with degree-zero unit, graded k-central left/right/bimodules, and degree-zero maps; internal shift `M{r}_d=M_{d-r}`. On the published commutative case, `{r}=(-r)` relative to `def-graded-ring-and-graded-module`. Internal grading is not super parity.. KS §2a, §2c.
items.strategy: Give all action laws, the k-centrality condition and finite-support direct sums. Unit and ground scalars have degree zero. Internal shift {r} equals the published twist (-r) in its commutative nonnegative special case. No super signs or differential are part of these definitions.

items.title: Graded module kernels cokernels and biproducts are degreewise
items.statement: The category of graded modules and degree-zero maps is abelian. Restrict ordinary kernels/images to homogeneous components, check induced quotient actions, and verify coimage→image degreewise; uses 18.1, `def-abelian-category`, and ordinary module isomorphism theorems.
items.strategy: For a degree-zero map f, kernels and images are sums of their homogeneous components; the quotient has component N_d/f(M_d). Construct kernel and cokernel universal maps degreewise. Hom groups are additive, finite direct sums are biproducts, and the ordinary first-isomorphism map is degree-zero with degree-zero inverse. Thus every mono/epi is normal/conormal. This works for all graded modules, not just finite modules over a possibly nonnoetherian algebra.

items.title: Graded balanced tensor product and homogeneous hom
items.statement: Grade the existing balanced quotient by total internal degree; define `Hom_d(P,M)` as A-linear maps raising degree by d and `HOM=direct sum_d Hom_d`. HOM consists of finite sums of homogeneous maps, not automatically all ungraded maps; degree-zero morphisms are Hom_0. No parity signs are inserted in multiplication merely from this grading.
items.strategy: Define the candidate total-degree tensor quotient by relations (ma) tensor x = m tensor (ax), without a sign. Define Hom_d as all ordinary A-linear maps of degree d and HOM as their direct sum. Each Hom_d allows maps on infinitely many source components; only the set of degrees d in an element of HOM has finite support. Grading well-definedness is established by the next lemma before using the construction.

items.title: Graded balanced tensor and shift isomorphisms
items.statement: Homogeneous balancing relations preserve degree; associativity, units, and `M{r} tensor N{s}=(M tensor N){r+s}` descend from the existing balanced maps. Check degrees and inverses; uses 18.3 and `thm-associativity-of-balanced-tensor-products`.
items.strategy: Present the balanced quotient using homogeneous generators and homogeneous relations; decompose arbitrary balancing relations into finite sums of these. This gives a direct grading and the graded balanced universal property. Tensor maps preserve degrees; associativity and units are the published explicit balanced maps and inverses. Tensor of two internal shifts raises total degree by their sum. Prove finite direct-sum distributivity by projections/inclusions or the balanced universal property, so later projective preservation has an explicit supplier.

items.title: Finitely generated graded projective module
items.statement: A graded left A-module is graded projective if it has the lifting property in the degree-zero abelian category. It is finite graded projective if it is also generated by finitely many homogeneous elements.
items.strategy: Define graded projective by degree-zero lifting against epimorphisms in the abelian category just proved; finite means finitely generated as a graded module. A finite ungraded generating family may be replaced by its finitely many homogeneous components. No blanket claim about arbitrary ungraded Hom maps.

items.title: Finite graded projectives are summands of finite graded free modules
items.statement: A homogeneous generating family gives a graded free epimorphism; projectivity splits it. Conversely graded free modules lift homogeneous generators and direct summands inherit lifting.
items.strategy: For homogeneous generators x_j of degrees r_j use the surjection direct-sum_j A{r_j} -> P. A projective P splits it. For the converse, lift the finitely many homogeneous basis elements through any degree-zero surjection, using the correct homogeneous component of any lift. A direct summand inherits lifting. This finite argument uses no infinite choice and asserts a supplied splitting, not a canonical one.

items.title: One sided flat module over an associative algebra
items.statement: For an associative unital algebra A, a right A-module M is flat if M tensor_A - from left A-modules to abelian groups is exact; a left A-module is flat with the tensor factors reversed. For a graded module, underlying-flat refers to this property after forgetting grading. Do not conflate it with an unstated graded-flatness equivalence.
items.strategy: Extend the commutative definition by declaring the tensoring side. Agreement in the commutative case follows from the balanced symmetry map. No ideal criterion or faithful-flatness assertion is imported.

items.title: Balanced tensor over an associative algebra is right exact
items.statement: For a B-A bimodule M over associative unital k-algebras, M tensor_A - is additive and right exact into left B-modules. For a graded M it is right exact on all graded left A-modules with degree-zero maps.
items.strategy: For X -> Y -> Z -> 0, the map to M tensor Z is onto by lifting each pure tensor. Identify (M tensor Y)/im(M tensor X) with M tensor Z by sending m tensor z to the class of m tensor y for any lift y. Lift independence follows from exactness; balancing and the inverse are explicit. In the graded case use homogeneous lifts and the previously proved grading. Preserve finite sums by the same universal property.

sources.locator: §24.8, tensor functor and Lemma 24.8.2; elementary quotient proof supplied locally

items.title: Bimodule tensor exactness and projective preservation
items.statement: For a B–A bimodule M, `M tensor_A -` is exact if M is right-A-flat. It sends finite projective left A-modules to finite projective left B-modules if M is finite projective on the LEFT B side. Prove the first by flatness and the second by applying tensor to split finite-free presentations. Graded version uses homogeneous presentations from 18.6.
items.strategy: Exactness follows from underlying right-A-flatness, with exactness detected on underlying groups and homogeneous components. Right exactness for associative A is supplied locally. If M is finite projective left B, apply tensor to P as a split summand of A^t: the same idempotent splitting exhibits M tensor_A P as a summand of M^t. In the graded case assume M finite graded projective on the LEFT B side, and use finite shifted-free presentations and shift/direct-sum isomorphisms. Finite sums and summands inherit projectivity by lifting; finite generation follows by projecting a finite generating family. The two hypotheses are independent, as the B witnesses calculate. For the ungraded finite case first form and split the finite free cover by the lifting definition; finite free modules lift a finite basis without AC. Do not import the arbitrary-free equivalence and its extra choice hypothesis.

items.title: Graded bimodule tensor hom adjunction
items.statement: For a B-A bimodule M, left A-module X and left B-module Y there is a natural bijection Hom_B(M tensor_A X,Y) = Hom_A(X,Hom_B(M,Y)), where the Hom terms in this ungraded assertion contain all ordinary module maps and (a f)(m)=f(ma). For graded modules the degree-d formula is Hom_d^B(M tensor_A X,Y) = Hom_d^A(X,HOM_B(M,Y)); in particular d=0 gives the adjunction between degree-zero graded module categories, and direct-summing gives the homogeneous-Hom version.
items.strategy: Prove the ungraded bimodule version directly from balanced maps; do not apply the published commutative adjunction outside its hypotheses. For a B-A bimodule M define left A-action (a f)(m)=f(ma); associativity follows from the right A-action. Curry F to x -> (m -> F(m tensor x)); inverse evaluates. Check B-linearity, A-balancing, outer action and naturality explicitly. In graded categories the right adjoint is HOM_B(M,Y), not Hom_0 alone: a homogeneous x of degree r gives a homogeneous map of degree r+d when F has degree d. Finite decompositions of x ensure a map into the direct-sum HOM even without finite generation of M. Obtain Hom_0 and each Hom_d adjunction, hence the HOM version. Ungraded Hom means all maps and need not equal underlying HOM.

items.title: Restriction and extension of scalars on graded module categories
items.statement: For a degree-zero algebra map A→B, restriction is exact and extension is its left adjoint. Extension is exact when B is right-A-flat and always preserves finite graded projectives, since it sends a summand of finite shifted copies of A to the corresponding summand of copies of B. Restriction preserves finite graded projectives when B is finite graded projective left A. Use 18.7–18.8 and inherit the ungraded scalar-change definitions.
items.strategy: First define scalar change for an arbitrary degree-zero unital k-algebra map A -> B, using the B-A and A-B actions from multiplication. This explicitly extends the published commutative definition. Restriction keeps the groups/components so is exact. Extension is left adjoint using evaluation HOM_B(B,Y) -> Y at 1 with inverse y -> (b -> by), and is right exact by the local tensor lemma. Exactness uses B right-A-flat. Tensor a finite shifted-free splitting to prove extension always preserves finite graded projectives. Restrict a finite shifted-free B splitting to prove preservation by restriction when B is finite graded projective LEFT A.

title: Graded Bimodules and Tensor Functors — Examples

items.title: Internal shift versus a change of degree
items.statement: For deg x=1 in k[x], the monomial x^j has degree j+2 in k[x]{2}, so (k[x]{2})_d=k[x]_(d-2), agreeing with the old twist k[x](-2).
items.strategy: Compute the components d<2, d=2 and d>2. Reassigning deg x=2 changes multiplication degrees, whereas an internal module shift leaves the algebra grading fixed. A shifted regular module is not asserted to be a unital graded algebra.

items.title: Right flat bimodule with nonprojective output
items.statement: Over a field k set A=k, B=k[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), M=k with left B action through augmentation and right scalar k action; all degrees zero. M is right-A-flat but M tensor_A A=k is not projective left B.
items.strategy: Tensor over k with M=k is the identity on vector spaces. The sequence 0 -> k -> B -> k -> 0 has injection 1 -> epsilon and augmentation quotient. A B-linear section s would satisfy s(1)=1+t epsilon and epsilon s(1)=0, contradicting epsilon nonzero. Thus the output fails projectivity, also in degree-zero graded modules.

sources.locator: §2b equation (2.1), separation of tensor hypotheses; elementary dual-number witness adapted locally

items.title: Left projective bimodule with nonexact tensor
items.statement: Over a field k set B=k, A=k[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), M=k with right A action through augmentation, all degrees zero. M is finite projective left B but M tensor_A - is not exact.
items.strategy: Use 0 -> k -> A -> k -> 0, 1 -> epsilon. Each tensor term is k, with k tensor_A A -> k given by u tensor a -> u augmentation(a), and k tensor_A k -> k by multiplication. The first map tensors to zero since 1 tensor epsilon=(1 epsilon) tensor 1=0, while the quotient tensors to the identity. This kills an injection and refutes exactness despite left projectivity.

sources.locator: §3.2 Definition 3.2.1; elementary dual-number witness adapted locally

items.title: Complex homotopy and contractibility in an additive category
items.statement: In an additive category define complexes, maps, homotopies, homotopy equivalences and contractibility using zero morphisms and the cochain convention f-g=dh+hd. Finite biproducts of complexes are degreewise by the published additive-complex theorem. No homology is defined without the additional abelian hypothesis.
items.strategy: Define cochain complexes with d:C^n -> C^(n+1), maps commuting with d, and homotopies h of degree -1 satisfying f-g=dh+hd. Homological reindexing C_n=C^(-n) makes h degree +1. Define equivalence and contractibility by identities. The published additive-complex theorem supplies degreewise finite biproducts; identify the abelian special case without asserting homology in an arbitrary additive category. The next lemma proves the homotopy calculus.

items.title: Additive complex homotopies form a composition compatible equivalence
items.statement: For complexes in any additive category, chain homotopy is an equivalence relation compatible with addition and pre/postcomposition by chain maps. Homotopy classes form an additive category; deleting a supplied contractible direct summand gives a homotopy equivalence.
items.strategy: Reflexivity uses 0, symmetry -h, transitivity h+k. Bilinearity gives the homotopy h+k for sums and u h v for compositions, since chain maps commute with differentials. These equations define the quotient without kernels. For X=Y direct-sum K and 1_K=d h_K+h_K d, use projection p, inclusion i and h=0 direct-sum h_K; then pi=1 and 1-ip=dh+hd. Compare the published abelian homotopy calculus only in its special case.

items.title: Invertible differential block and schur complement reduction
items.statement: Fix the ordered cochain block convention above. Retain every object outside degrees n,n+1, replace those degrees by A,B, retain the adjacent surviving blocks, and propose `dbar^n=a-b phi^(-1)c`. State the homological reindexing dictionary.
items.strategy: Use ordered source A direct-sum U and target B direct-sum V, rows B,V and columns A,U. Require an actual two-sided inverse phi^(-1):V -> U. Propose the reduced objects A,B with neighbouring surviving maps p,r and middle a-b phi^(-1)c. Square-zero is an obligation discharged in the next lemma, not an assumption of the definition.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1, Lemmas A.1–A.2; arXiv PDF pp.68–69

items.title: Block triangular basis changes diagonalize an invertible differential block
items.statement: Put `L=[[1,-b phi^(-1)],[0,1]]` on `B direct-sum V` and `R=[[1,0],[-phi^(-1)c,1]]` on `A direct-sum U`. Multiply explicitly to get `L d^n R=diag(a-b phi^(-1)c,phi)`, and print `L^(-1),R^(-1)`. If `d^(n-1)=[p;q]` and `d^(n+1)=[r,s]`, use `d^2=0` to obtain `cp+phi q=0` and `rb+s phi=0`; after the basis changes the neighbour maps are `[p;0]` and `[r,0]`. This proves the proposed reduced arrows still square to zero, rather than assuming it from the Schur formula.
items.strategy: Write L=[[1,-b phi^(-1)],[0,1]], L^(-1)=[[1,b phi^(-1)],[0,1]], R=[[1,0],[-phi^(-1)c,1]], R^(-1)=[[1,0],[phi^(-1)c,1]]. Ordered multiplication gives LdR=diag(a-b phi^(-1)c,phi). If the neighbours are [p;q] and [r,s], d^2=0 gives q=-phi^(-1)cp and s=-rb phi^(-1). Therefore R^(-1)[p;q]=[p;0], [r,s]L^(-1)=[r,0], and the reduced arrows square to zero including the outer adjacent equations.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1, Lemmas A.1–A.2; arXiv PDF pp.68–69

items.title: Homological gaussian elimination splits off a contractible two term complex
items.statement: Define the chain isomorphism by `T^n=R^(-1)=[[1,0],[phi^(-1)c,1]]`, `T^(n+1)=L`, and identities elsewhere. Row 24.3 identifies the transformed complex with the direct sum of the reduced complex and `0->U --phi-> V->0`. Give the inverse matrices and contraction `phi^(-1):V->U` of the second summand. This is a chain isomorphism followed by deletion of a contractible summand, not an equality of the original and reduced complexes.
items.strategy: Take T^n=R^(-1), T^(n+1)=L and identities elsewhere, with the displayed inverses. The transformed differential T^(n+1)d(T^n)^(-1) and neighbours identify the transformed complex with reduced complex direct-sum (U -> V). Contract the latter by phi^(-1):V -> U; transport through T. No boundedness or abelian assumption is needed.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1, Lemmas A.1–A.2; arXiv PDF pp.68–69

items.title: Homological gaussian elimination gives a strong deformation retract
items.statement: For the original complex X and reduction Xbar, print `p^n=[1,0]`, `p^(n+1)=[1,-b phi^(-1)]`, `i^n=[1;-phi^(-1)c]`, and `i^(n+1)=[1;0]`, with identities elsewhere. Let only `h^(n+1):B direct-sum V->A direct-sum U` be nonzero, `h^(n+1)=[[0,0],[0,phi^(-1)]]`. Verify componentwise `pi=1`, `1-ip=dh+hd`, and the side conditions `ph=0`, `hi=0`, `h^2=0`. This fixes both map direction and signs and upgrades a bare homology comparison to chosen deformation-retract data.
items.strategy: Print p^n=[1,0], p^(n+1)=[1,-b phi^(-1)], i^n=[1;-phi^(-1)c], i^(n+1)=[1;0]; elsewhere identities. The only nonzero h is h^(n+1)=[[0,0],[0,phi^(-1)]]. Verify chain maps using the neighbour equations. pi=1. At degree n, hd=[[0,0],[phi^(-1)c,1]]=1-ip; at degree n+1, dh=[[0,b phi^(-1)],[0,1]]=1-ip; elsewhere both vanish. Matrix multiplication gives ph=hi=h^2=0. All composites are typed.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1, Lemmas A.1–A.2; arXiv PDF pp.68–69

items.title: Homological gaussian elimination preserves homotopy type and homology
items.statement: The maps in 24.5 are a chain-homotopy equivalence in every additive category. When the ambient category is abelian so the published homology objects exist, they induce inverse homology isomorphisms. Do not infer an isomorphism of complexes before the contractible summand is split off.
items.strategy: Use the chosen maps and identity homotopies from the retract. In an abelian category only, reindex to the published chain convention and apply the homotopy-equivalence/quasi-isomorphism theorem. The result is an isomorphism of homology objects, not of original complexes.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1, Lemmas A.1–A.2; arXiv PDF pp.68–69

items.title: Finite iterated homological gaussian elimination
items.statement: A finite sequence of cancellations is licensed when each selected block is invertible in the CURRENT Schur-complement complex. Compose retracts recursively by `(p,i,h)=(p_2 p_1,i_1 i_2,h_1+i_1 h_2 p_1)` and verify the retract identities and side conditions. Alternatively, any finite aggregate block `Phi:U->V` may be cancelled at once when `Phi` itself is invertible. Different valid choices yield complexes homotopy equivalent to the original, not canonically equal or generally identical to one another. Infinite cancellation is not asserted without termination or extra local-nilpotence/completeness data; even finiteness does not guarantee a smaller presentation.
items.strategy: For two retracts compose p=p2 p1, i=i1 i2 and h=h1+i1 h2 p1. Expand dh+hd=(1-i1p1)+i1(1-i2p2)p1=1-ip. Use p1i1=1 and the two sets of side conditions to get pi=1, ph=hi=h^2=0 (both cross terms in h^2 vanish). Induct on the finite supplied sequence. Test pivot invertibility anew in the current reduced complex. A finite aggregate invertible block also satisfies the one-step theorem. No claim of termination of an infinite process, guaranteed simplification, canonical choice or identical final presentations.

items.title: Additive functors preserve chosen homological gaussian cancellations
items.statement: An additive functor preserves finite biproducts, negatives, isomorphisms and their inverses, so it carries the block formula, `p,i,h`, and the chosen cancellation to the corresponding cancellation of the image complex. Exactness is unnecessary for preservation of the homotopy equivalence; it is needed only for separate claims comparing pre-existing homology objects.
items.strategy: An additive functor takes identities, sums, negatives, composition and inverse pairs to the same equations, and transports the chosen finite biproduct diagrams by the published theorem. Thus it transports dbar,p,i,h and their equations. No exactness is used; comparison F(H(X))=H(F(X)) is a separate abelian-category exactness question.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1, Lemmas A.1–A.2; arXiv PDF pp.68–69

items.title: Transfer of chain maps across gaussian reductions and naturality limits
items.statement: For chosen retracts of X and Y, transfer a chain map f by `fbar=p_Y f i_X`; transfer a homotopy similarly. Identity transfers strictly, while `(g f)bar` and `gbar fbar` differ by the explicit null-homotopy obtained from `1-i_Y p_Y=d h_Y+h_Y d`. Thus transfer is functorial on homotopy classes, but not generally a strict functor on chain maps. It is strictly natural for morphisms preserving the chosen summands and commuting with the pivot/retract data. The construction depends on the decompositions and pivot, so no choice-free naturality or confluence theorem is claimed.
items.strategy: For f:X -> Y transfer fbar=pY f iX. A homotopy s transfers to pY s iX. Identities transfer strictly. For X ->f Y ->g Z, bar(gf)-barg barf = pZ g(1-iY pY)f iX = dH+Hd with H=pZ g hY f iX. Thus composition holds on homotopy classes. If f iX=iY fbar and pY f=fbar pX (and the chosen pivot data commute), transfer is strictly compatible on this restricted class. Decompositions are supplied, not canonical.

items.title: A two by two unit pivot fixes the minus schur sign
items.statement: The two-term rational cochain complex Q^2 -> Q^2 with differential [[1,1],[1,1]] reduces at the lower-right unit to Q -> Q with zero differential.
items.strategy: Compute 1-1=0 and the chosen p,i,h. Kernel and cokernel of the rank-one differential are each Q; the wrong plus sign yields multiplication by 2 and zero kernel/cokernel. Thus it changes both cohomology groups.

items.title: Neighbouring differentials after a gaussian basis change
items.statement: For k -> k^2 -> k^2 -> k with maps [1;-1], [[1,1],[1,1]], [1,-1], cancellation reduces the sequence to k -> k -> k -> k with maps 1,0,1.
items.strategy: Both original adjacent composites vanish. With L=[[1,-1],[0,1]] and R^(-1)=[[1,0],[1,1]], neighbours become [1;0] and [1,0]; the middle becomes diag(0,1). Print p,i,h and verify the side conditions as an instance of the general theorem, in every characteristic.

items.title: Two finite cancellation orders and their composite retracts
items.statement: In the CMW Lemma A.2 configuration C^n=B direct-sum C, C^(n+1)=D1 direct-sum D2 direct-sum E, C^(n+2)=F direct-sum G, cancel psi:B -> D1 and phi:D2 -> F. In either order the surviving differentials are delta-gamma psi^(-1) beta and nu-mu phi^(-1) lambda.
items.strategy: Write d^n=[[psi,beta],[u,v],[gamma,delta]] and d^(n+1)=[[x,phi,lambda],[y,mu,nu]]. All letters are typed morphisms and d^2=0. Cancelling psi first leaves phi unchanged; cancelling phi first leaves psi unchanged. Composite projections on the three degrees are [0,1],[-gamma psi^(-1),0,1],[-mu phi^(-1),1], inclusions are [-psi^(-1)beta;1],[0;-phi^(-1)lambda;1],[0;1]. Check both orders give these matrices using x psi+phi u+lambda gamma=0 and the other square-zero equations. Calculate the composite homotopy in each order from h1+i1 h2 p1; print the resulting blocks rather than infer identical h from identical p,i. Outer maps are [bullet;alpha] and [bullet,eta], reduced to alpha and eta. Only this configuration is order-independent. In both orders h^(n+1)=[[psi^(-1),0,0],[0,0,0]] and h^(n+2)=[[0,0],[phi^(-1),0],[0,0]] in the displayed original decompositions. These are the two nonzero blocks; they have zero composite. Compare the maps explicitly after substituting the square-zero equations.

sources.locator: Appendix A.1 Lemma A.2, arXiv PDF p.69 / printed p.68

items.title: A nonunit differential entry cannot be gaussian cancelled
items.statement: Deleting 0 -> Z --2-> Z -> 0 cannot preserve its homotopy type: its degree-one cohomology is Z/2.
items.strategy: Compute kernel zero and cokernel Z/2. A contraction would require an integer endomorphism h with 2h=1, impossible. The pivot has no inverse in Ab even though nonzero.

sources.locator: §1.4, homotopy versus acyclicity; integer witness is a local specialization

items.title: Gaussian reduction is not strictly natural for arbitrary chain maps
items.statement: Let X=Y direct-sum K where Y and K are both Q --1-> Q in degrees 0,1. Cancel K. Chain endomorphisms f=[[0,0],[1,0]] and g=[[0,1],[0,0]], identical in both degrees, transfer to zero, but gf transfers to 1_Y.
items.strategy: The differential on X is diag(1,1), so both matrices are chain maps. Projection and inclusion of Y give pf i=pg i=0 and p g f i=1_Y. The identity is a nonzero chain map and is null-homotopic via h^1=1. This refutes strict composition preservation, while the homotopy-category statement survives.
